description: Machine-readable inventory of every default and checkpoint validation gate. Dependency-free JSON: read it with the standard library. This catalog owns collection descriptions and measured counts; README owns operator commands and approximate timing prose.

baseline.method: each gate run once, serially, from a clean worktree; wall time measured around the process
baseline.ci_reference_status: OPEN. Node 22 and Python 3.12 are not installed on the reference machine (available: node 23/24/25/26, python 3.13/3.14). Every approximate_seconds value below is local Node 26.7.0 / Python 3.14.7 evidence and is explicitly NOT the CI baseline the specification asks Checkpoint 0 to record. Capturing the CI-version baseline requires a workflow run or an approved local toolchain install.
baseline.python_collection_note: Measured by `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q --collect-only` on 2026-08-17, before tests/test_validation_catalog.py was added (which brings it to 751). README previously hand-maintained 678, which was stale; README now points here.
baseline.python_serial_total_note: Sum of 37 pre-existing files run one process each. About 40 minutes. Three owners account for 74.5%: test_workbook_manager (810.34s), test_verify_workbook_candidate (694.43s), test_workbook_manager_import_projection (222.91s).
baseline.node_baseline_result: 298 pass, 7 fail across 6 files (all 16 files). Restricted to the fourteen documented readiness gates: 298 tests, 292 pass, 6 fail across 5 files — an exact match for the specification's 2026-08-17 audit.

checkpoint_1.method: same method as the Checkpoint 0 baseline: each gate run once, serially, one process per file, wall time measured around the process. Same machine and runtimes.

Removing the duplicate schema invocation accounts for 64.06 s of the reduction; the data-derived seatbelt sweeps, which now read the workbook for their expected side, give back about 5 s. Three runs of the full set measured 53.27 s, 54.56 s and this one — wall times, not budgets. A hard timing budget needs three stable baselines (spec §5, Layer 1).

workbook_manager.selection_policy: Select the entire workbook_manager group when any member requiring verified_manager_fixture is selected; run it in one pytest process so the process-wide verified projection/candidate build is paid once.

No full checkpoint re-timing was performed for this metadata correction.

gates.disposition_reason: The §7 catalog contract test. Fails when a default/checkpoint test file has no catalog entry, when two entries claim one named acceptance lock, when a generating gate lacks an isolated output declaration, when a gate claims read_only or in_process while naming writes, when a protected-output gate — or a SUITE that would run one — is assigned unsafe parallel execution, or when README disagrees with the catalog. Each condition is proved by a forced failure so the check is never green for the wrong reason. Suite membership is derived from the command, not trusted from gate_ids, and file discovery is recursive.
gates.notes: Checkpoint 4 review added the read_only/in_process honesty check. Every other isolation assertion branches on `generates`, so a gate declaring generates:false escaped all of them — which is how three Node gates came to claim read_only while writing temp workbook and workbook-truth copies.

modeling_notes: No gate declares intentional_product_acceptance_lock as its PRIMARY authority. Locks attach to gates through the acceptance_locks field and are tracked as behaviors in the coverage ledger. stingray-form-regression owns the dealer lock but its dominant job is runtime state, so that is what it declares. When Checkpoint 1 splits the dealer lock out of that 2,949-line file, the split-out owner should declare the lock class directly. Deliberate choice, recorded so a later reader does not read it as an omission.

Two of the six documented stale assertions have SIBLING assertions in the same test encoding the same superseded decision: stingray-form-regression.test.mjs:2859 and z06-runtime-rule-corrections.test.mjs:238. Those siblings currently PASS, which makes them the dangerous ones — a rewrite that fixes only the failing line leaves the superseded behavior pinned.

approximate_seconds is wall time for one process per gate. A single pytest invocation over several files is faster than the sum, because interpreter startup and workbook import are paid once. Compare like with like before claiming an improvement.

mutation_canaries.method: A throwaway `git worktree` at HEAD with the Checkpoint 1 test files copied in. Each canary mutates a COPY of the workbook (or injects a defect into a copy of the generator/runtime) inside that worktree; the canonical workbook and the working tree are never touched. The worktree is removed afterwards.
mutation_canaries.scope_note: Spec §8 lists eight canaries. Checkpoint 1's acceptance names three (asset URL, override count, registry membership); those three plus seven forced-failure proofs of the new assertions were run here. The last two were added after PR review, which caught the Stingray sweep deriving its expectations from the payload under test — an omission no canary had been run against. Canaries 4, 6 and 8 belong to later checkpoints and were NOT run.

checkpoint_2.method: A throwaway detached `git worktree` at the Checkpoint 2 commit. Generator defects were injected into that worktree's copy of the generator, the affected model regenerated into a temporary output root, and the parity gate run against it; registry canaries used mutated copies of data.js and of the workbook. `git checkout -- .` reset the worktree between canaries and the worktree was removed afterwards. The canonical workbook, the working tree, and the tracked artifacts were never mutated.
checkpoint_2.scope_note: Checkpoint 2's acceptance asks for oracle independence proved by injected mismatch (spec §8 canary 5). Ten injected-defect canaries were run plus both halves of §8 canary 1 against the widened media sweep. Each defect had to fail its OWN assertion and no unrelated one — a parity suite where one defect fails six tests is not localizing anything. Canaries 4, 6 and 8 belong to later checkpoints and were NOT run.
